blockers.likely_cause: I agree with the merger. The burst's light reaches every puff of its own cloud with no self-shadowing, and the non-fire path of CombatParticleMix spreads one cooled yellow colour evenly over the cloud. At dusk CombatNight and flashHold cut the burst's flash from its birth, so the fireball body is dim. The ground term (combatBallCosine) still lights a band of plain from the same light. Fix ideas: let the burst light cross its own cloud (as CombatSmokeTransmittance does for fire). Let it fall off faster on its smoke. Give the young burst an emissive core so the visible fireball is always brighter than the ground it lights.

blockers.problem: A white wall. The test sets fog 0.3 (a morning mist). Original and landed show green grass, a rock outcrop and a tree line. The overhaul paints about 85% of the frame one flat pale grey with a slight cool cast. Grass 10 to 20 m away is already grey. The rock is gone and the trees are faint ghosts. At thumbnail it reads as washed out, not as more real. AI sight follows this fog, so a light-mist mission also becomes a short-range fight. This is unchanged since round 2; the plate fix only removed the warm band.

blockers.likely_cause: Under a grey sky the volumetric medium for setFog 0.3, including the near-ground and valley mist, is far denser than the classic fog distance the mission asked for. The grey-sky apply then sinks everything into one air colour. Tune the mist density so that fog 0.3 keeps roughly the original's visible range, with the rock and tree line legible. Keep the Target.cpp fog-sight link as it is.
